detail: Pre-correction baseline: C105 TEST_DRIFT; C116 PRODUCT_DEFECT; C125 OUT_OF_SCOPE; C126 TEST_DRIFT.
Four shared-residue JobId mismatches, one invalid second-finalizer wait, and one query against the wrong migration-history schema; no product credit.
Provider-finalize-race hypothesis was false; successor command trace located abort handling after the losing seal call.
Unchanged C116 contract returned Sealed plus PreparationConflict.
Final characterization rerun of the same C116 contract RED; not a distinct defect.
Removing post-seal discovery makes packet, retained, and provider-finalized rediscovery assertions fail.
Disabling recovery-aware RecordAsync restores stale-revision failures on retryable, terminal, and host-level paths.
Rethrowing the known acquire-lost-race conflict stops the losing host.
Supplying the wrong exact fingerprint restores PreparationConflict in both original and recovery C116 assertions.
Removing the SQL fingerprint comparison changes ExactMismatch to Claimed.
Removing owner/generation enforcement from defer lets a displaced claimant release the successor claim.
Removing owner/generation enforcement from finalize lets a displaced claimant complete the successor claim.
Legacy durable-work-source test still migrated only to the 20260923 selector and rejected the new Sealer capability; successor test targets the current migration and passes.
One of two same-Job SDK cases observed a disposed unpooled Npgsql data source; both exact cases pass independently in retained successor runs.

Initial combined correction run: five ambiguous SQL-name failures, two readiness-drift failures, two timing timeouts, three intermediate C116/fingerprint/selection assertions, one acquire-host observation race, and one expiry-fixture setup failure; all have named successor runs.
Intermediate correction run: two readiness-drift failures, two repeated C116 failures, and one expiry-fixture deadline-constraint failure; superseded by targeted successors.
Targeted intermediate run retained the expiry-fixture deadline-constraint failure and a C126 expectation drift; both corrected in successors.
Diagnostic replay of the known C116 PreparationConflict before the exact committed-recovery correction; no distinct product credit.
Second diagnostic replay of the same known C116 PreparationConflict; no distinct product credit.
Third diagnostic replay of the same known C116 PreparationConflict; no distinct product credit.
Early F1 smoke reached StateConflict before the recovery SQL shape stabilized.
Early F1 smoke exposed an invalid integer LEAST expression; corrected before the retained restored gate.
Early F1 smoke exposed an ambiguous PL/pgSQL identifier; corrected before the retained restored gate.
Intermediate migration round failed before the intended trigger assertion because fixture dependencies were not seeded; successor migration proof passes.
First retained-mode proof lacked the complete raw-export catalogue fixture; successor covers both supported retained modes.
Removing pre-RecordPending exact recovery restores PreparationConflict, and disabling the bounded mixed-queue turn starves recovery behind normal work.
Removing mandatory NULL rejection and sampling lease time before row locks makes both direct capability and lock-wait proofs fail.

The combined runtime plus migration filter ran Down/Reapply against the same PostgreSQL fixture while runtime cases were active; separate retained migration and runtime gates supersede this invalid combined schedule.
The first deterministic C116 proof depended on an uncontrolled winner/loser start race and timed out before the loser reached provider reuse; the successor controls both sides of the exact race.

The durable exact-reuse path correctly used Inspect:Prepared while the old assertion accepted only the equivalent Prepare:ExistingMatch path; the successor asserts either exact provider-reuse route while retaining the durable residue checks.

The stale acquire contender was allowed to repoll and claim the winner's newly sealed recovery before the winner completed; the successor test harness parks only that losing contender and leaves production scheduling unchanged.
74/74 failed test results classified across thirty-one retained failed runs; repeated characterization and intermediate harness failures are not distinct product defects.
